title: Manchester United’s wage bill falls year-on-year, latest financial results show
content:
Manchester United’s wage bill fell by £14million ($18.9m) compared to the previous year, according to the Old Trafford club’s second-quarter financial results.

United offloaded several of their highest-earning players during the summer transfer window, with Marcus Rashford and Andre Onana joining Barcelona and Trabzonspor on loan respectively.

As well as allowing Alejandro Garnacho and Antony to leave permanently, while loaning Rasmus Hojlund to Napoli, staff also continued to leave United as part of the restructuring programme implemented by co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the INEOS-led hierarchy.

As a result, United’s latest results reveal that their wage bill for the three months ending December 31 totalled £75.1m, a nine per cent decrease compared to the same period last season, despite the summer arrivals of Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko, Diego Leon and Senne Lammens.

United’s wages to revenue ratio — already one of the healthiest in the Premier League — subsequently fell to 45 per cent, down from 47.6 per cent.

United announced an operating profit of £32.6m for the first six months of the 2025-26 season, but that included £48.2m profit from player sales. The underlying result exclusive of those, a total which is more commonly used in the football industry as a club’s operating result, was a £15.7m loss. That was still a £1.5m improvement on a season ago, but underlying profitability remains elusive, with continued high transfer expenditure and falling revenues restricting the impact of cuts elsewhere.

Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, said in a release that the results demonstrated “the positive financial impact of our off-pitch transformation materialise both in our costs and profitability.

“We continue to take a football-first approach and invest in both our men’s and women’s first teams.

“Today’s results demonstrate the underlying strength of our business as we continue to push for the best football results possible for our men’s and women’s teams.”

Despite a pre-interest and tax profit of £32.6m, the club’s best such second-quarter result since before the Covid-19 pandemic, United still posted a £2.5m loss for the first six months of the financial year at the bottom line.

United’s total revenues fell to £330.7m, compared to £341.8m over the same period last year, due to sharp falls in both commercial and matchday income.

Commercial income stood at £78.5m for the second quarter, a 7.8 per cent drop year-on-year, and is down by 4.5 per cent over the first six months of the campaign.

As recently revealed by The Athletic, concerns have been raised internally at the club over United’s commercial performance amid the lack of a training kit sponsor. A £24m deal with blockchain company Tezos expired last summer and is yet to be replaced.

United attributed the fall in matchday revenues to fewer games at Old Trafford following last season’s failure to qualify for European competition and this season’s elimination from the Carabao Cup. United’s £75.7m gate receipts in the first six months of this season were just £2.8m below a year ago, when they played five more games at Old Trafford. On a per-game basis, matchday income was up by 45 per cent to £7.6m. The big leap reflects both a rise in ticket prices and all home games this season being in the Premier League, as opposed to the less lucrative Carabao Cup (two home games in 2024-25).

While wage savings will continue to accrue across the season, United’s improvement at the bottom line to the end of December was largely driven by a better summer of player sales. The club’s underlying result improved by nine per cent but remains in the red, even after significant spending cuts.

That reflects a year of declining revenues, inevitably driven by last season’s underperformance on the pitch. United reiterated a revenue projection of £640m-£660m for 2025-26, down from 2024-25’s club record £666.5m.

Running up until December 31, United’s initial second-quarter results did not reveal the amount of compensation paid to Ruben Amorim and his coaching staff following their dismissal on January 5.
